A surjection from the complement coordinate group (size >= chi) onto color labels makes each original outcome attainable from every prescribed action; all transitions remain in every selected neighbourhood. The finite checker exhaustively tests 845 admissible two-agent frames on three outcomes and several boundaries. The theorem claims sufficiency only; no all-size inference from finite tests.

value.rationale: The joint-intersection conflict graph has a clear mathematical role: only outcomes that may compete inside one complete profile need distinct control labels. It yields a genuinely instance-sensitive action budget, replacing the established total-outcome-range guarantee with chi of the co-occurrence graph. For a natural star family of n+1 outcomes, two copies suffice for every n, rather than the n+1 universal guarantee. This is a nontrivial structural constructive refinement, not an arbitrary invariant or a small finite census.
